issues.t: Automatic transmission slips, jerks or fails
issues.sym: Slipping when accelerating, engine revs flaring between gears, jerky or delayed shifts, or the van losing forward drive.
issues.why: The automatic transmissions in this generation wear their internal clutches, often linked to overheating, and the wrong fluid makes it worse. Transmission complaints are the costliest Quest problems for these years.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or jerks, have it diagnosed before it fails completely. Use only the fluid Nissan specifies.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle or whine from worn guides
issues.sym: A rattle for a few seconds after a cold start, a rattle or whine from the front of the engine at certain speeds, and sometimes a check engine light with cam timing codes.
issues.why: The timing chain guides and tensioners on the 3.5L V6 wear, and sludge from skipped oil changes can make the tensioners stick.
issues.next: Have a mechanic listen to it and read any codes. Fix it before the chain jumps; the job usually includes the water pump and front seal.

issues.t: Power sliding door stops working or will not close
issues.sym: A sliding door that stops partway, grinds, will not latch shut, or does not move at all with the button.
issues.why: The door motor wears out, the drive cables break, or the latch fails.
issues.next: If a door will not latch, turn off the power door switch and close it by hand until it is repaired. Do not drive with a door that may open.

issues.t: Front subframe rusts through
issues.sym: Clunks from the front end, visible rust holes in the frame under the engine, or a failed safety inspection.
issues.why: The front subframe that carries the engine and suspension can rot from road salt, usually near 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the subframe inspected on a lift. Severe rust is a safety risk and the subframe must be replaced.

issues.t: Center dash display and gauges go blank
issues.sym: The center-mounted display shows dashes or goes blank, gauges cut in and out, or segments look dim or broken.
issues.why: Connections on the gauge cluster circuit board and display ribbon fail with age.
issues.next: Have the cluster repaired or replaced by a cluster repair specialist or dealer.

issues.t: Water leaks from clogged SkyView or sunroof drains
issues.sym: Wet headliner, damp carpets, or water dripping inside after rain.
issues.why: The glass roof panels have drain tubes that clog or kink, so water backs up into the cabin.
issues.next: Have the drains cleared with air or a flexible line and dry the interior quickly to prevent mold and electrical damage.

issues.t: Front wheel bearings hum or growl
issues.sym: A hum or growl that gets louder with speed and may change when you turn.
issues.why: Owners of many Quests report front wheel bearings and hubs wearing out, sometimes on both sides.
issues.next: Have a shop check for play and noise. A failing bearing should be replaced before it seizes.

issues.t: Front control arms, ball joints and tie rods wear early
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, loose steering, wandering, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The front control arm bushings, ball joints and tie rod ends on these heavy vans wear out, and owners report replacing them more than once.
issues.next: Have the front end checked for play and get an alignment after any parts are replaced.

issues.t: Alternator stops charging
issues.sym: A battery or charging light, dim lights, or a dead battery.
issues.why: Owners report alternator failures, sometimes more than once, on both the 2004-2009 and 2011-2013 Quests.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested before replacing the battery.

issues.t: Cam or crank position sensor failure
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough running, stalling, or the engine cranking without starting.
issues.why: Camshaft and crankshaft position sensors on the 3.5L V6 fail, and owners often replace more than one.
issues.next: Have the codes read. These sensors are usually quick to replace.

issues.t: Worn engine mounts cause thumping
issues.sym: A thump or clunk felt in the floor when you shift into gear, accelerate, or brake, and extra vibration at idle.
issues.why: Engine mounts wear or crack and let the engine move too much.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected. Replacing a broken mount stops the thumping and protects other parts.

issues.t: Distributor shaft bearing seizes and the engine stalls
issues.sym: The engine stalls suddenly or cranks but will not start.
issues.why: The bearing on the distributor shaft can rust and seize, which stops the spark.
issues.next: Have a mechanic check for spark. Replacing the distributor is the usual fix.

issues.t: Oil leaks from valve cover and oil pan gaskets
issues.sym: Oil spots under the van, a burning oil smell, or oil on the engine.
issues.why: Owners report the valve cover, oil pan and other gaskets leaking as the engine ages.
issues.next: Have the source found and the gasket replaced before oil drips onto the exhaust.

issues.t: Power steering hose wears through and leaks
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaking, a whining pump, or steering that gets heavy.
issues.why: Owners report the power steering pressure hose rubbing through or leaking, along with other power steering line leaks.
issues.next: Top up the fluid and have the leaking hose replaced quickly so the pump is not damaged.

issues.t: Torn CV axle boots and clicking axles
issues.sym: Clicking when turning, grease thrown inside the wheel, or vibration when accelerating.
issues.why: The rubber boots on the front drive axles split, the grease escapes, and the joints wear out.
issues.next: Replace a torn boot or the axle soon, before the joint fails and leaves you stranded.

issues.t: CVT jerks, hesitates or fails
issues.sym: Jerking or hesitation when accelerating, a whining sound, loss of power, or a transmission that stops working.
issues.why: The continuously variable transmission (CVT) in this generation is the most reported Quest problem, with failures at around 90,000-110,000 miles.
issues.next: Change the CVT fluid on schedule and have any jerking checked early. Ask a Nissan dealer about any warranty help for your VIN.

issues.t: Rear A/C leaks and stops cooling
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, especially in the back, or needs recharging again and again.
issues.why: The long A/C lines to the rear of the van corrode and leak, or the rear evaporator or valve fails. A rear leak drains the front system too.
issues.next: Have the A/C leak-tested with dye or a sniffer before paying for a recharge.

issues.t: Fuel pump software can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls at low speed or idle, mostly with a quarter tank or less.
issues.why: Programming in the fuel pump control module can fail to supply enough fuel when the tank is low.
issues.next: Have the free reprogramming done and keep the tank above a quarter until then.

issues.t: Brake pedal pivot pin can slip out (recall)
issues.sym: The pedal feels unusual and stopping power drops.
issues.why: The pedal pivot pin was not formed to spec and can slide partly out.
issues.next: Get the free repair right away.

issues.t: Steering wheel emblem can break off in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs.
issues.why: The emblem on the driver airbag cover can crack and fly off when the airbag deploys.
issues.next: Have the airbag cover replaced for free.

issues.t: Power sliding door may not latch in cold weather (recall)
issues.sym: The sliding door does not fully latch, especially when it is cold.
issues.why: The door actuator can bind in the cold, so the door may not latch and could open.
issues.next: Have the free repair done.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor may not switch the airbag correctly (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag status light acts strangely or stays on with a child seated.
issues.why: The front passenger seat occupant sensor did not meet the advanced airbag rule.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and recalibrate or replace the sensor.

issues.t: Third-row seat latch bracket can break (recall)
issues.sym: The third-row seat does not stay latched.
issues.why: A weld on the third-row seat striker bracket can break.
issues.next: Have the free repair done.

issues.t: Second-row seat can pinch fingers (recall)
issues.sym: Fingers can get caught when adjusting the second-row seat.
issues.why: Moving parts in the seat adjuster are exposed.
issues.next: Have the free covers and parts installed.

issues.t: Fuel tank vent hose can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell near the rear of the van.
issues.why: The fuel tank vent hose can crack and leak fuel, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Have the free hose replacement done.

issues.t: Power windows work after the key is off (recall)
issues.sym: Windows can still be raised after the engine is shut off and a door is opened.
issues.why: The power window circuit does not cut out as the safety rule requires, which can trap a child.
issues.next: Have the free repair done.

issues.t: Battery post can leak acid and fail (recall)
issues.sym: Acid or corrosion around the negative battery post, or a sour smell.
issues.why: A defective negative post can leak acid and fail, risking fire or explosion.
issues.next: Have the battery checked and replaced under the recall.

issues.t: Steering rack bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Loose steering, clunks over bumps, or vibration.
issues.why: Rack-and-pinion mounting bolts may not have been tightened properly at the factory.
issues.next: Have the free inspection done.

issues.t: Fuel tank straps can break (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell or a tank that sags.
issues.why: The spot welds on the fuel tank straps can break.
issues.next: Have the straps replaced for free.

issues.t: Second-row captain’s chair may not latch (recall)
issues.sym: The right second-row seat slides.
issues.why: The seat latch can stay unlatched.
issues.next: Have the free repair done.

issues.t: Seat belt buckle bases may be weak (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs.
issues.why: Some buckle bases were not heat-treated properly.
issues.next: Have the free buckle replacement done.

issues.t: Front seat belt buckle bolt can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A loose front seat belt buckle.
issues.why: Trim can trap the buckle bolt so it is not tight.
issues.next: Have the free repair done.
